Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Solvex is excited about the latency guarantees and the routing options. Procurement here has two asks before we can issue a PO:

1) We need Redwood to accept a weekly invoice cadence for consumption billing (we run weekly accounting cycles). Is that possible, or do you require a monthly consolidated invoice?

2) Our PO template requires a) a project code string (PROJ-SOLVEX-XXXX), b) a funding BU code, and c) a Billing Entity ID to map into our ERP. We need the vendor to echo those fields on every invoice.

3) Net terms: our standard is net60, but we can move to net45 for strategic vendors. If Redwood needs net30 or a prepay, please state what’s required so we can route internally for approval.

I’ve attached our PO template (Solvex_PO_Template.xlsx) — you’ll see the required fields. Please confirm what you can support and any contract wording we should include.

Hi Lydia — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front: yes, we can support weekly invoices, and we can echo the PO fields you listed, with a couple of governance items. Details below and a proposed next step.

What we can support:
- PO fields: We can surface Project Code, Funding BU, and Billing Entity ID on every invoice if the PO includes them in fields we can parse (PO number in subject + an "InvoiceTo" line or structured PO metadata). Preferred PO number format: RWD-<ENTITY>-<6digits> (we can accept any numeric suffix but need the vendor-side Billing Entity ID to map invoices).
- Weekly invoices: Allowed. We will generate a weekly line-item invoice (CSV + PDF) and a consolidated monthly statement for reconciliation.
- Net terms: Standard is net30 for self-serve/hosted customers. Our finance team will allow net45 on a case-by-case basis for committed or enterprise deals. For net45 we require either (a) a one-time prepay equal to 25–30% of the first-month estimated spend or (b) a signed finance exception (internal approval).

Proposed options to keep things moving quickly:
1) Solvex issues a standard PO with the three required fields present and the PO number visible on each invoice. We accept weekly invoices as individual bill runs and will expose a monthly consolidated statement for reconciliation.
2) For net45 terms: either 30% prepay (applied as credit to the first invoice) OR we initiate an internal finance exception / credit check. If you prefer not to prepay, let us know and I’ll loop in Jordan from Finance for a rapid exception.

Next step: if you’re OK with option 1 + (choose prepay or exception), I’ll send a DocuSign amendment and a short mutual action plan to hit your 2026-08-20 target. Attaching our invoice guidance for your AP team.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks for the ping — quick internal notes from Finance:

1) Weekly invoices + monthly consolidated statement: doable. We’ll publish a weekly CSV/ PDF line-item and an automatically generated month-to-date consolidated statement with invoice references (suitable for ERP ingest). We’ll need the Billing Entity ID placed as an invoice-level custom field so our export maps to Solvex’s ERP.

2) Net45 / prepay: Standard approval threshold for net45 without additional credit is $150k TCV. For this opportunity (est. first-year $540k if ramps), we can sign net45 with a 30% initial credit hold (applied against first invoice) and a finance exception memo logged. If Solvex can commit to a 12-month prepay arrangement we can remove holdback; otherwise holdback stands for the first 60 days.

3) PO format: Require PO number and Billing Entity ID in the PO header; we can parse these from either the PO PDF or an accompanying metadata JSON/CSV. Recommend they supply PO as structured fields in the email for straight-through processing.

Action items I’ll take: prepare a short finance-exception doc and a DocuSign amendment (I’ll cc Legal). Marissa — can you confirm contract language that captures the holdback and invoice cadence?

Jordan Blake
